data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'azza' which means 'to be strong, to support'. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Azza usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, supportive and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It is a powerful name for a girl child, signifying strength, support, and resilience. In Arab cultures, the naming of children is an important tradition, and the name chosen reflects the parents' hopes and aspirations for their child. By choosing the name 'Azza', parents are expressing their hope that their daughter will grow up to be a strong and resilient individual who is able to support herself and her loved ones.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the name 'Azza' is also associated with Aisha bint Abu Bakr, one of the most revered and beloved wives of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). Aisha was known for her intelligence, wit, and strength of character. She was a scholar in her own right, known for her extensive knowledge of Islamic law and Hadith. By choosing the name 'Azza' for a child, parents may be inspired by the example of Aisha and hope that their daughter will embody the qualities of intelligence, strength, and character that Aisha exemplified. Additionally, using the name of a beloved and revered figure in Islamic history can help instill a sense of pride and connection to the rich history and traditions of the Islamic faith.
